problem_type: benchmark gesture enters React Flow's frame-rate-driven auto-pan band, so a hardcoded post-gesture assertion becomes a coin flip across substrates
symptom: Quality Gate job `Canvas Performance (Linux)` reported red on commits that do not touch canvas code (main 930db4cd, run 33967545326; branch commit 5f266afd, run 33956782546). Both artifacts fail with `marquee selected only 8 nodes` while every measured timing budget passed (max frameGapP95 29.9 ms against a 33 ms darwin ceiling and a 53 ms Linux ceiling). The same benchmark reproduced locally on darwin/arm64, alternating between 9 and 12 selected nodes across runs of identical code, fixture and window size.
direct_cause: The marquee-select gesture ended at `stage edge - 10px` and started from a blank point at ratio 0.03 of the stage, both inside React Flow's 40px auto-pan band (`calcAutoPan(pos, bounds, speed = 15, distance = 40)` in @xyflow/system 0.0.81). While the pointer sits in that band, `Pane.autoPan()` pans the viewport once per `requestAnimationFrame`, so the swept region grows by an amount proportional to how many frames the machine rendered during the gesture. Measured viewport pan on three consecutive darwin runs of identical code: (-95.8, -113.8) -> 12 selected, (-49.9, -62.0) -> 9 selected, (-49.9, -62.5) -> 9 selected. The reliability guard compared that frame-rate-dependent count against the literal constant 12.
class_root: The benchmark asserted a hardcoded expectation against a gesture whose swept region was not reproducible. Nothing owned the invariant that a benchmark pointer gesture must sweep a deterministic region, and nothing derived the post-gesture expectation from the region actually swept, so a constant tuned on one substrate silently became a frame-rate measurement on every other substrate.
affected_population: Every Quality Gate `Canvas Performance (Linux)` run of the medium canvas profile, on any commit including ones that do not touch canvas code
Local darwin benchmark runs, which reproduce the same 9/12 alternation
Any future benchmark scenario whose pointer gesture reaches within 40px of the React Flow pane edge while a selection or node drag is active

external_sources.purpose: calcAutoPan(pos, bounds, speed = 15, distance = 40) is the source of the 40px auto-pan band and the 15px-per-frame pan speed that AUTO_PAN_SAFE_MARGIN_PX is derived from; verified against the installed @xyflow/system 0.0.81 bundle in node_modules.

Pane.autoPan() runs on requestAnimationFrame, autoPanOnSelection defaults to true, and selectionMode defaults to SelectionMode.Full; verified against the installed @xyflow/react bundle, and Nomi overrides none of the three.

invariants: A benchmark pointer gesture stays inside the auto-pan safe area, so the region it sweeps is a function of stage geometry alone and contains no time-dependent term.
The auto-pan safe margin is derived from @xyflow/system's calcAutoPan distance default, not from a hand-tuned constant.
A post-gesture selection expectation is derived from the region actually swept, never written as a literal node count.
Selection expectations use React Flow's SelectionMode.Full semantics and express sub-pixel boundary disagreement as a definite/possible interval, so a real over- or under-selection still fails.
A stage too small to contain the safe area fails closed instead of producing a non-reproducible measurement.

The non-degeneracy check is dimensionless: it measures how much of the reachable node band the sweep covered, so it does not drift with stage size the way a swept-area-over-safe-area ratio does (0.941 on a 1200x790 stage vs 0.583 on a wider one for the same fixture).
generality_proof: Every benchmark gesture that needs a reproducible swept region resolves its start point through findCanvasBlankPoint's inset option and its end point through clampIntoAutoPanSafeArea, both reading the single AUTO_PAN_SAFE_MARGIN_PX derived from the library constant. Every post-gesture selection verdict is built from expectedFullySelected over the same swept rectangle the gesture used, and the guard fails closed when a sample carries no derived expectation, so no caller can fall back to a literal count. autoPanSafeArea throws when the stage cannot contain the safe area, so a shrinking window surfaces as an explicit error rather than as a silently non-reproducible sweep. check:canvas-gesture-determinism then makes both writing shapes unwritable across the whole canvas benchmark tree: it was verified red against the pre-fix file (flagging the stage-edge endpoint and `selected < 12`) and green against the repaired file. The mechanism itself was verified end to end: viewport pan during marquee-select measured (0,0) on every run after the change, against a (-95.8,-113.8) / (-49.9,-62.0) spread before it.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own where a benchmark gesture may travel and what its swept region implies, so both the gesture and its expectation are derived from geometry rather than from a tuned constant.
Own blank-point discovery for all canvas gestures and let a caller demand a start point outside the auto-pan band, returning null so the caller fails closed when none exists.

Fail the build when a benchmark drag endpoint is written against the stage edge inside the auto-pan band, or when a swept-region selection verdict is compared with a numeric literal instead of a derived expectation.

same_class_entry_points.entry_point: runAction marquee-select and its sampleHardFailures guard
same_class_entry_points.evidence: This is the reported failure. Start point now comes from findBlank with inset AUTO_PAN_SAFE_MARGIN_PX, end point from clampIntoAutoPanSafeArea, expectation from expectedFullySelected over the swept rect. Measured after the change: selected 9, expected 9-9, nodeBandCoverage 1.0, identical across 8 runs in two separate processes, with viewport pan delta (0,0).

same_class_entry_points.entry_point: runMultiNodeDrag selection guard and the node-drag gestures
same_class_entry_points.evidence: Instrumented the viewport transform around every drag scenario on darwin: node-drag-image, node-drag-video, multi-node-drag and drag-over-dense-edges all recorded a pan delta of exactly (0,0) on both runs, so these gestures never enter the auto-pan band. Their selection is also established by discrete clicks rather than by a swept region, so no count depends on pan distance.

Recorded pan delta (300, 197.5) identical on both runs, which is the scenario's own deliberate zoomOutTo(page, 0.45) call rather than auto-pan. A time-integrated auto-pan would differ run to run, as marquee-select did before the fix.

same_class_entry_points.entry_point: PERFORMANCE_BUDGETS timing ceilings and the non-darwin calibration factor
same_class_entry_points.evidence: The platform-aware timing calibration already landed on main in e24dc8e84. Both failing Linux artifacts passed every timing budget: the worst measured frameGapP95 was 29.9 ms against a 33 ms darwin ceiling and the 53 ms Linux ceiling, and the worst longTaskP95 was 55 ms against 80/128 ms. No budget change is part of this repair.

recurrence.reason: The mechanism is a frame-rate-integrated viewport pan, so it re-fires on every run of the job and on every machine, and it has already produced two independent red Quality Gate runs on 2026-09-05 plus a local darwin reproduction. Any future scenario whose gesture reaches the pane edge would acquire the same non-reproducibility, and any future literal count assertion over a swept region would acquire the same false-red.
same_class_scan: Searched tests/ux and src for data-selected consumers: found the marquee guard, click-select domainSelected, the blank-click selectedAfterClear read, and dragScenarios.mjs runMultiNodeDrag. Only the marquee guard compares a swept-region count against a literal.

Searched src for selectionMode, SelectionMode, autoPanOnSelection, selectionOnDrag and selectNodesOnDrag: production code overrides none of them, so React Flow's defaults (SelectionMode.Full, autoPanOnSelection true, 40px band, 15px per frame) are the ones in force.

Instrumented the viewport transform around runAction for node-drag-image, node-drag-video, multi-node-drag, drag-over-dense-edges, drag-at-low-zoom and marquee-select on darwin, two runs each, to separate gestures that auto-pan from gestures that do not.

Compared the two red Linux artifacts (run 33967545326 commit 930db4cd, run 33956782546 commit 5f266afd) against every scenario verdict in each: all timing and activation budgets passed in both; the sole failure in each was the marquee count, once as a warmup sample and once as a measured sample.

prevention.invariant: A benchmark drag endpoint is produced by clampIntoAutoPanSafeArea rather than by subtracting a literal from the stage edge; a swept-region selection verdict is compared with an expectation derived from the region actually swept; and the non-degeneracy check is dimensionless so it does not become a second platform-dependent threshold.
prevention.failure_mode: check:canvas-gesture-determinism exits non-zero with the offending file, line and expression; it is hard-zero with no ratchet baseline and no debt registry. At runtime autoPanSafeArea throws when the stage cannot contain the safe area, the inset blank-point search returns null so the caller throws, and a marquee sample carrying no derived expectation is recorded as a hard failure instead of passing by default.
prevention.strategy: Put the auto-pan band width, the safe area, the clamp, the swept rectangle and the SelectionMode.Full expectation interval in one pure module derived from the library constant; make the gesture and its verdict read from that module; and add a hard-zero static gate to the gates chain so the two writing shapes that produced this false red cannot be reintroduced.

legacy_paths.rationale: The literal `selected < 12` guard and the `stage edge - 10px` gesture endpoint are deleted in the same change. No caller can select the old behaviour: the guard now fails closed when a sample carries no derived expectation, so a reverted gesture cannot pass silently.

dependency_lifecycle.current: @xyflow/react 12.x with @xyflow/system 0.0.81 (calcAutoPan distance 40px, speed 15px per frame, autoPanOnSelection true, selectionMode Full)
dependency_lifecycle.target: Stay on the installed @xyflow line; re-verify the auto-pan constants on every @xyflow upgrade rather than upgrading away from the behaviour.
dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The auto-pan behaviour is correct for real users, so there is nothing to upgrade away from; the benchmark simply must not measure inside the band. The retained risk is that a future @xyflow release changes calcAutoPan's distance default and silently shrinks our safe margin.
exit_criteria: On any @xyflow/react or @xyflow/system upgrade, re-read calcAutoPan's distance and speed defaults and update REACT_FLOW_AUTO_PAN_EDGE_PX to match.
After such an upgrade, re-run the marquee-select scenario and confirm the recorded viewport pan delta is still (0,0) on every run; a non-zero delta means the band grew past AUTO_PAN_SAFE_MARGIN_PX.
Confirm React Flow still defaults selectionMode to Full; if it changes to Partial, expectedFullySelected must switch to intersection semantics.

migration: No persisted user data and no production code changes. Existing committed benchmark baselines remain readable. New marquee-select samples record mountedNodeCount, expectedSelection, nodeBandCoverage and the swept rect, so an artifact from a future red run states directly what was swept and what was expected.
residual_risks: The auto-pan-free marquee sweeps a slightly smaller region than the pre-fix gesture did, so marquee-select frame timings are not directly comparable with baselines recorded before this change. Measured darwin frameGapP95 after the fix is 10.3-10.7 ms against a 33 ms ceiling, so no budget is at risk; the comparability caveat applies only to historical marquee-select deltas.

The Linux reading for the repaired gesture is proven only by the CI run on this branch. The darwin reading is 9 selected / 9-9 expected / 1.0 node-band coverage, stable across 8 runs in two processes. The Linux stage is a different size, so its absolute selected count will differ by design; what must hold on both is that the count equals the derived expectation and does not vary between runs.

check:canvas-gesture-determinism recognises a drag endpoint either inside a dragPath(...) call or on a variable-assignment line. A point built across several statements and only then passed to dragPath would escape the static rule; the runtime fail-closed guard and the derived expectation remain the second line of defence.

Rule 2 is scoped to scenarios whose selection comes from a swept region, currently only marquee-select. multi-node-drag still compares its click-established selection with a literal 2; that count does not depend on pan distance (measured pan delta (0,0)), so it is out of this failure class and deliberately untouched.
